slot.topic_title: Setting Up a Test for a Population Mean or Population Mean Difference

item.title: Setting Up a Test of a Claimed Mean Bulb Life
item.stimulus: A company claims that its light bulbs last a mean of 1200 hours. A consumer group suspects the true mean lifetime is less than 1200 hours. The group buys a random sample of 40 bulbs from the thousands in stores nationwide and tests each one. The sample mean lifetime is 1168 hours and the sample standard deviation is 96 hours.

parts.prompt: Define the parameter of interest and state the null and alternative hypotheses for the test.

criteria.text: Defines μ as the true mean lifetime, in hours, of all of this company's light bulbs sold in stores nationwide.
criteria.evidence: Response defines μ as the true mean lifetime, in hours, of all of this company's light bulbs sold in stores nationwide, naming the response variable and the population in context.
criteria.fix: Name the parameter with its symbol and say which population mean (or mean difference) it is, in context.

criteria.text: States H₀: μ = 1200 and Hₐ: μ < 1200.
criteria.evidence: Response writes H₀: μ = 1200 and Hₐ: μ < 1200, with the alternative in the correct direction.
criteria.fix: Write the null with an equals sign and take the direction of the alternative from the question being investigated.

parts.prompt: Identify the appropriate procedure and show that its conditions are met.

criteria.text: Identifies the appropriate procedure as a one-sample t-test for a population mean.
criteria.evidence: Response names a one-sample t-test for a population mean.
criteria.fix: Name the procedure from the data design: one sample, matched pairs (analyze the differences), or two independent samples.

criteria.text: Checks the randomization condition: the 40 bulbs were randomly selected.
criteria.evidence: Response states the randomization condition in context: the 40 bulbs were randomly selected.
criteria.fix: Check that the data came from random selection or random assignment, and say how, in context.

criteria.text: Checks the 10% condition: 40 bulbs are less than 10% of all of this company's bulbs in stores.
criteria.evidence: Response checks that the sample size is less than 10% of the population: 40 bulbs are less than 10% of all of this company's bulbs in stores.
criteria.fix: When sampling without replacement, compare each sample size with 10% of its population to confirm independence.

criteria.text: Checks the sample-data condition: n = 40 is at least 30, so the sampling distribution of the sample mean is approximately normal.
criteria.evidence: Response states the sample-data condition and why it is met: n = 40 is at least 30, so the sampling distribution of the sample mean is approximately normal.
criteria.fix: State the condition that applies: sample sizes of at least 30, or samples with no strong skewness or outliers.

item.model_answer:
(a) μ is the true mean lifetime, in hours, of all of this company's light bulbs sold in stores nationwide. H₀: μ = 1200 versus Hₐ: μ < 1200.

(b) The procedure is a one-sample t-test for a population mean, Randomization: the 40 bulbs were randomly selected. 10% condition: 40 bulbs are less than 10% of all of this company's bulbs in stores. Sample-data condition: n = 40 is at least 30, so the sampling distribution of the sample mean is approximately normal.
item.verification_python:
mu0, n = 1200, 40
assert n >= 30
assert 1168 < mu0
print("ALL_CHECKS_PASSED")
